risk_if_not_implemented: Without Status Reporting To Governing Body, security, compliance and resilience activities may lack direction, ownership and executive support, leaving required controls unperformed. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Lack of oversight of internal controls (R-GV-6), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), Unreliable Assurance / Decision Information (R-GV-10), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Data Quality Degradation / Data Poisoning (MT-12), Conflict of Interest (COI) / Undue Influence / Insider Misconduct (MT-15).

compensating_control_1.name: Measures of Performance
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to develop, report and monitor Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP) measures of performance.
compensating_control_1.justification: Measures of Performance (GOV-12) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Status Reporting To Governing Body (GOV-09.1) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Executive Leadership Oversight of Security, Compliance & Resilience Controls
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to provide a security, compliance and resilience controls oversight function that reports to the organization's executive leadership.
compensating_control_2.justification: Executive Leadership Oversight of Security, Compliance & Resilience Controls (CPL-07) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Status Reporting To Governing Body (GOV-09.1) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
